title: Six Faults and a Matrix: Which Check Catches Which Fault, and the Faults That Only One Check Sees

questions.question: A suite is green. What does that say about whether it would catch a flipped sign in the controller?
options: Nothing: a test that has never failed has never been shown able to, and the way to find out is to put the fault in
questions.explanation: All three checks passed on the clean run.

questions.question: What does detection_matrix record as caught?
options: A check that passes on a faulty run
A fault that a check finds, that is, a check that fails on that faulty run
questions.explanation: caught[f][c] is true when check c returns false on faulty run f.

questions.question: In the table, which faults were seen by exactly one check?
options: The flipped sign and the weak actuator (by the response check) and the removed limiter (by the limit check)

questions.question: What is lost if the response check is removed, the limit check, and the model check?
questions.explanation: The model check duplicates what the response check sees, and says why.

questions.question: The response check is loosened to ends within 0.6 of the target. What happens?
options: The weak actuator, which ends 0.2 away, is missed by every check, and 4 of the 6 faults are left on a single check
questions.explanation: Re-run the table after every change to a bound.

questions.question: What does the fault table not show?
options: Faults you did not think of, and faults of other sizes: it shows only that the ones put in are caught
questions.explanation: Six faults are a start and not a proof.
